analysis: Examined three changed files: .github/workflows/docs-impact.yml, changelog.d/ci-git-swiftpm-cache.md and docs/developer/build.md. The only executable change is docs-impact.yml lines 61-68, which adds filter: blob:none and a non-cone sparse-checkout excluding docs/reports/**/*.gz and landing/public/**/*.mp4. The job still checks out the PR head SHA with read-only contents permission and no secrets, and it still runs the same scripts. The checkout is partial, so scripts/docs-impact-check.py (not supplied) may fetch blobs lazily. It could mis-evaluate if it reads the excluded .gz or .mp4 paths. That affects CI documentation-gate correctness and is not a provider threat-model boundary. The changelog and build.md are documentation. They describe CI cache behavior: saves only on master and dev pushes, PR restores of base-branch entries, persist-credentials: false, and a fallback to a cold checkout. Those claims cannot be verified here because ci.yml and the provider-ci-build action are not in the supplied units. The cache-poisoning and trust-boundary implications live in those unseen files. Only the patch excerpt for ci.yml behavior is described in prose, so the next pass should examine it if it is in another batch. Provider threat IDs (TB-002, TB-011, A-015..A-017) are not touched: no provider runtime, attestation, key custody, coordinator protocol or encrypted-cache code changed. The docs add a push-time route request to the Darkbloom sandbox plane, which admits branches itself. That is an external contract outside the supplied evidence, and I record it as unverified, not as a finding. No concrete security regression was identified in the supplied units.
